summary: A Saturday evening pedestrian market along Wua Lai Road, just south of Chiang Mai’s old city. The traditional silverworking quarter lends the market a craft focus alongside local food, clothing and souvenirs. It is a compact alternative to Chiang Mai’s larger Sunday Walking Street.
whyGo: Browse the historic silversmith district and look for locally made silverware and other crafts.
Sample casual street food and shop among local visitors and travelers in an evening setting.
bestFor: A low-planning Saturday evening stroll, food sampling and craft browsing.
Travelers staying in or near the old city who want a weekend market without booking a tour.
skipIf: You cannot visit on Saturday evening; this is a weekly market, not an everyday night market.
Dense pedestrian crowds, slow browsing or limited step-free movement would make the visit uncomfortable.
duration: Allow about 1–2 hours for a relaxed walk and food stops; this is a planning estimate and depends on crowds and how far you browse.
cost: No admission charge is listed; budget separately for food, drinks and purchases. Stall prices vary, and no current official price list was found.
hours: Chiang Mai Municipality lists Saturdays, 17:00–22:00. A Tourism Authority of Thailand listing gives approximately 17:00–22:00; treat these as published hours and recheck locally for December 2026.
bestTime: Arrive near the 17:00 opening for more room to browse, or later for the full evening atmosphere. Crowd levels by hour are not officially published.
gettingThere: The market runs along Wua Lai Road near Chiang Mai Gate, just outside the old city; the Tourism Authority of Thailand says it is a short walk from the gate. Walk from nearby accommodation or use a local taxi/songthaew and agree the drop-off before the street becomes busy. Expect road closures or diversions around market time; no official transit or parking plan was found.
booking: No booking or admission ticket is indicated. Go directly; bring cash for small purchases and food, as stall payment options vary.
accessibility: No official accessibility information was found. The market occupies a busy street and can become tightly crowded; curb cuts, accessible toilets, seating and step-free routes are unconfirmed. Contact a local tourism office or accommodation for current access advice if needed.
practicalTips: Use Chiang Mai Gate as the navigation landmark and confirm your return pickup point before entering the crowded market.
Carry small cash and keep valuables secure in the crowd.
Ask permission before photographing vendors or their work; check silver purity, weight and price before buying.
Wear comfortable shoes and allow time to move slowly when the street is busy.
decemberNotes: December 2026 Saturdays fall on the 5th, 12th, 19th and 26th. The published schedule is weekly, but no dated December 2026 market notice or holiday exception was found. Confirm locally before setting out, especially around holiday weekends; do not assume a special Christmas or New Year program.
uncertainties: The weekly 17:00–22:00 hours come from current municipal and tourism-board listings; day-to-day stall participation and temporary closures are not guaranteed.
No official guidance located for current transport changes, accessibility, toilets, or typical spend.
The Tourism Authority of Thailand image is an illustrative market reference; its page does not state a reuse license.
